label: <DEL> step, about to recall first token from {c,f,q,n,l,s,w,z,1,y,0,d}
explanation: Mostly a delimiter-step unit: 66% of activation mass is at the <DEL> step (31% of delimiter steps fire), where the model must output original token 0. Whether it fires there and how strongly depends on that first token: c, f, q, n, l, s, w fire most (about 80% precision for that subset), with weaker firing for z, 1, y, 0, d. The largest activations (near max) are on <DEL> with first token c. Delimiter firing is also more likely in short sequences (L 3-5). The rest of the mass (about 28%) is weak firing during the original phase, mostly on first occurrences of input g or p (also i, j), and peaks around t=4-5. Almost silent during the copy phase beyond recall_idx 1, and never fires once copying has gone wrong. The predicate misses the original-phase g/p firing and the scattered delimiter firing for other first tokens. Adding a clause for g/p in the original phase raises F1 only to 0.55, so this is not a clean explanation.
